conventions.convention: The local space is real P1 on a nondegenerate d-simplex, d ≥ 2; the degree of freedom is the normalized facet integral and its dual polynomial is 1 − dλ_i.

The global domain is bounded, connected, Lipschitz polyhedral and has a finite matching affine simplicial mesh. Interior facet means agree; boundary facet means vanish. Pointwise continuity is not imposed.

Fractional regularity uses the local Gagliardo double integral, with diagonal integrand zero and almost-everywhere classes. H^(1+r) requires first weak derivatives in H^r; r = 1 is interpreted as W^(2,2). Countable Choice is assumed.
Normal-gradient traces are L² facet functions only under the stated strict regularity threshold 1/2 < r ≤ 1. Green's identity uses outward cell normals and f = −Δu.

The comparison space is H¹₀(Ω) + V_h. Its squared norm is the broken gradient square plus the sum of h_F^−1 times squared facet jumps. Interior jumps use either fixed cell ordering; boundary jumps are the cell trace. The load satisfies f ∈ L²(Ω).

A Dirichlet Poisson smoothing index is a conditional domain property for every L² datum, with 1/2 < s ≤ 1 and a full H^(1+s) bound by C_reg times the datum norm; it is not asserted for every bounded domain.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, H^r functions on a shape-regular simplex have bounded L² facet traces for 1/2 < r ≤ 1, with face-mean fluctuation bounded by C h_K^(r−1/2)[q]_(H^r(K)). If u ∈ H¹(K), ∇u ∈ H^r(K), and f = −Δu ∈ L²(K), the stated cellwise Green identity holds for every H¹(K) test. Global H¹ traces match across interior facets, H¹₀ traces vanish on boundary facets, and global H^r traces match for 1/2 < r < 1.

Under Countable Choice on a shape-regular affine mesh, for 1/2 < r ≤ 1 and u ∈ H^(1+r)(K), the face-average interpolant reproduces P1 and satisfies gradient error ≤ C h_K^r |u|_(H^(1+r)(K)), L² error ≤ C h_K^(1+r) |u|_(H^(1+r)(K)), and h_F^−1/2 times facet error ≤ C h_K^r |u|_(H^(1+r)(K)). For u ∈ H¹₀(Ω), the global interpolant belongs to V_h^(CR,0).

Assume Countable Choice. For every matching shape-regular simplicial mesh and v_h ∈ V_h^(CR,0), the sum over interior and boundary facets of h_F^−1 ||[v_h]_F||²_(L²(F)) is at most C ||∇_h v_h||²_(L²(Ω)), with C depending only on d and shape regularity.

For the stated regular zero-boundary solution with 1/2 < r ≤ 1 and L² load, |R_h(u;v_h)| ≤ C h^r |u|_(H^(1+r)) ||∇_h v_h||₂. If also ζ ∈ H¹₀ ∩ H^(1+s), 1/2 < s ≤ 1, then |R_h(u;I_h ζ)| ≤ C h^(r+s) |u|_(H^(1+r)) |ζ|_(H^(1+s)).

Under Countable Choice on the stated bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain and finite matching shape-regular mesh, each v_h has a continuous piecewise affine companion E_h v_h ∈ H¹₀(Ω), with ||∇E_h v_h||₂ ≤ C ||∇_h v_h||₂ and ||v_h − E_h v_h||₂ ≤ C h ||∇_h v_h||₂.

Under Countable Choice, for 1/2 < r ≤ 1 and u ∈ H¹₀(Ω) ∩ H^(1+r)(Ω) solving −Δu = f ∈ L²(Ω) on the stated domain, any finite matching shape-regular mesh gives ||u − u_h||_(sharp,h) ≤ C h^r |u|_(H^(1+r)(Ω)).
